children: JGBs edge lower in price terms in the early Tokyo session ahead of Japanese Finance Ministry's auction today of about 700 billion yen of 20-year government bonds, which will be a reopening of the October 2026 issue. "Current levels look cheap relative to fair value based on interest rate risk supply-demand," two analysts of Barclays' FICC Research say in a note."Given that recent reports on defense spending and consumption tax cuts [in Japan] appear unlikely to lead to large-scale additional JGB issuance, the auction should offer some appeal," the analysts add. The yield on the five-year JGBs is up 0.5 bps at 2.265%. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
